message.content:
**Short answer:**  
Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but it isn’t handled by a “local council” in the way that a UK city council would. In Atlanta, noise complaints are typically taken by the **Atlanta Police Department (APD)** or the **City of Atlanta’s Code Enforcement** office. You can also bring the issue to your local city council member if you want a more formal or political follow‑up.

---

## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta

| Step | What to Do | Where / How |
|------|------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Call 311** | Dial **311** from any phone (or 404‑656‑3111 if calling from outside the city). 311 is the city’s non‑emergency hotline and will route your complaint to the appropriate department. |
| 2 | **File Online** | Visit the City of Atlanta’s 311 portal: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> and select “Noise Complaint.”  You’ll be asked to provide details such as location, time, and description of the noise. |
| 3 | **Contact APD Directly** | If the noise is urgent or you want a quicker response, call the APD’s Noise Complaint line: **404‑656‑3111**. |
| 4 | **Use the City’s Code Enforcement** | For ongoing or repeated noise issues (e.g., construction, parties, commercial noise), you can file a complaint with the City’s Code Enforcement office: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> or call 404‑656‑3111. |
| 5 | **Reach Out to Your City Council Member** | If you feel the issue isn’t being addressed, contact your local council member’s office.  City council members in Atlanta are elected representatives who can advocate on your behalf.  Find your council member here: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/city-council>. |

---

## Key Ordinances & Resources

| Resource | What It Covers |
|----------|----------------|
| **Atlanta Municipal Code – Title 10, Chapter 10.2 (Noise)** | Sets limits on allowable noise levels, hours of operation, and penalties for violations. |
| **Atlanta Police Department – Noise Complaint Procedure** | Provides guidelines for reporting and handling noise complaints. |
| **City of Atlanta 311 Portal** | Central hub for all non‑emergency city services, including noise complaints. |
| **City Council Contact List** | Allows you to identify and contact the council member representing your precinct. |

---

## Practical Tips

1. **Document the Noise** – If possible, record the noise (audio or video) and note the date, time, and location. This evidence can help the authorities assess the complaint.
2. **Be Specific** – Describe the type of noise (construction, music, barking dogs, etc.) and how it violates the city’s noise ordinance.
3. **Follow Up** – If you don’t hear back within a few days, call 311 or the APD again. Keep a record of your complaint number and any correspondence.
4. **Escalate if Needed** – If the noise persists after the initial complaint, you can file a second complaint or contact your city council member for additional support.

---

### Quick Reference

| Action | Phone | Website |
|--------|-------|---------|
| 311 (non‑emergency) | 404‑656‑3111 | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> |
| Noise Complaint (online) | N/A | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> |
| City Council | 404‑656‑3111 (for general inquiries) | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/city-council> |

---

**Bottom line:**  
You can definitely report a noise complaint in Atlanta. Use the 311 system, the APD’s noise line, or the City’s Code Enforcement office. If you want a more formal or political avenue, contact your local city council member. All of these channels are designed to address noise issues and enforce the city’s noise ordinances.
